title: Overloading versus overriding across compile time and runtime
answer: Overloading is resolved before runtime: the compiler selects a method signature from the declared argument types and applicable conversions. If that selected signature is an instance method that is overridden, runtime dynamic dispatch can then choose the implementation belonging to the actual object. In other words, overload selection determines which signature is called; overriding may determine which implementation of that signature executes.
